429, retryable;
the detached scan finishes
and stores its verdict" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="60" width="240" x="820" y="790" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="o_note" parent="1" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=10;fontColor=#666666;" value="The retryable answer is 429 and not 503 on purpose: pip auto-retries a 503, which would bury the message. 503 is reserved for Unverifiable, where retrying immediately is pointless. The URL in the BLOCKED phrase is what makes a refusal actionable, so the phrase builder reserves bytes for it and shortens the code instead." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="50" width="1020" x="40" y="865" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="inv" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;strokeWidth=2;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=11;fontColor=#9c2b25;fontStyle=1;spacingLeft=10;spacingTop=6;whiteSpace=wrap;" value="THE INVARIANT
A check that could not run is Unverifiable, never a serve, and it is never stored as a durable Blocked verdict. Storing it would refuse the artifact forever over a broken check, and would tell a developer 'we found malware' about something nothing examined. Each scan also decodes under one ScanRules snapshot, so a SIGHUP landing mid-scan cannot swap the policy a verdict was produced under." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="80" width="1020" x="40" y="935" div.div: pip talks only to the proxy. The simple index is rewritten so every artifact link comes back here, and Scanner::decide is the one place that answers yes or no.

div.div:
IN PROGRESS
429, retryable;
the detached scan finishes
and stores its verdict

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 852px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#666666, #959595); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: The retryable answer is 429 and not 503 on purpose: pip auto-retries a 503, which would bury the message. 503 is reserved for Unverifiable, where retrying immediately is pointless. The URL in the BLOCKED phrase is what makes a refusal actionable, so the phrase builder reserves bytes for it and shortens the code instead.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(248, 206, 204), rgb(81, 45, 43)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(184, 84, 80), rgb(215, 129, 126));

display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#9c2b25, #ff9f9a); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
THE INVARIANT
A check that could not run is Unverifiable, never a serve, and it is never stored as a durable Blocked verdict. Storing it would refuse the artifact forever over a broken check, and would tell a developer 'we found malware' about something nothing examined. Each scan also decodes under one ScanRules snapshot, so a SIGHUP landing mid-scan cannot swap the policy a verdict was produced under.
